title: No $k$-critical graph has $k+1$ vertices
statement: Let $G$ be a finite graph on a nonempty vertex set $V$. If $G$ is $k$-critical — that is, $G$ has chromatic number $\chi(G) = k$ and every proper subgraph $H$ of $G$ satisfies $\chi(H) < \chi(G)$ — then $G$ does not have exactly $k+1$ vertices; that is, $\abs{V} \neq k+1$.
hypotheses_covered: G is k-critical (chromatic number k and critical)
replaced:
\emph{Deduce that no \texttt{k}-critical graph
has exactly \texttt{k + 1} vertices.}
